From db5b4e39c4e63700c68a7e65fc4e1f1375273476 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 17:35:50 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ip6_gre: make ip6gre_header() robust

Over the years, syzbot found many ways to crash the kernel
in ip6gre_header() [1].

This involves team or bonding drivers ability to dynamically
change their dev->needed_headroom and/or dev->hard_header_len

In this particular crash mld_newpack() allocated an skb
with a too small reserve/headroom, and by the time mld_sendpack()
was called, syzbot managed to attach an ip6gre device.

[1]
skbuff: skb_under_panic: text:ffffffff8a1d69a8 len:136 put:40 head:ffff888059bc7000 data:ffff888059bc6fe8 tail:0x70 end:0x6c0 dev:team0

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
index c82a75510c0e..8bc3f05f594e 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
@@ -1366,9 +1366,16 @@ static int ip6gre_header(struct sk_buff *skb, struct net_device *dev,
 {
 	struct ip6_tnl *t = netdev_priv(dev);
 	struct ipv6hdr *ipv6h;
+	int needed;
 	__be16 *p;
 
-	ipv6h = skb_push(skb, t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h));
+	needed = t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h);
+	if (skb_headroom(skb) < needed &&
+	    pskb_expand_head(skb, HH_DATA_ALIGN(needed - skb_headroom(skb)),
+			     0, GFP_ATOMIC))
+		return -needed;
+
+	ipv6h = skb_push(skb, needed);
 	ip6_flow_hdr(ipv6h, 0, ip6_make_flowlabel(dev_net(dev), skb,
 						  t->fl.u.ip6.flowlabel,
 						  true, &t->fl.u.ip6));
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c`

- **Added variable `needed`**: Stores the total header length (`t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h)`) to avoid repeated calculation.
- **Added headroom check and expansion**: Before calling `skb_push()`, the function now checks if `skb_headroom(skb) < needed`. If true, it attempts to expand the headroom using `pskb_expand_head()`. If expansion fails, the function returns `-needed` (an error indicating the required size).
- **Updated `skb_push()`**: Replaced the hard-coded expression with the `needed` variable.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The core fix addresses a crash (`skb_under_panic`) that occurred when `ip6gre_header()` called `skb_push()` on an skb with insufficient headroom. The headroom could become too small because external devices (e.g., team/bonding) can dynamically change `dev->needed_headroom` or `dev->hard_header_len` after the skb was allocated. The addition of the headroom check and `pskb_expand_head()` ensures that the skb is resized to accommodate the required header before `skb_push()` is invoked, preventing the buffer underrun. The use of the `needed` variable makes the code cleaner and avoids repeating the header size calculation. Together, these changes make `ip6gre_header()` robust against dynamic headroom changes and eliminate the crash condition.

Fixes: c12b395a4664 ("gre: Support GRE over IPv6")
Reported-by: syzbot+43a2ebcf2a64b1102d64@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/693b002c.a70a0220.33cd7b.0033.GAE@google.com/T/#u

Here is the root cause:
The ip6gre_header() function in ip6_gre.c did not check or expand the skb headroom before calling skb_push(), causing skb_under_panic when the required header length exceeded available headroom. This occurred because team/bonding drivers can dynamically change dev->needed_headroom or dev->hard_header_len after skb allocation, or because skbs allocated for other protocols (e.g., mld packets) were later used for ip6gre encapsulation with insufficient reserved space.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int ip6gre_header(struct sk_buff *skb, struct net_device *dev,
 			 unsigned short type, const void *daddr,
 			 const void *saddr, unsigned int len)
 {
 	struct ip6_tnl *t = netdev_priv(dev);
 	struct ipv6hdr *ipv6h;
+	int needed;
 	__be16 *p;
 
-	ipv6h = skb_push(skb, t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h));
+	needed = t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h);
+	if (skb_headroom(skb) < needed &&
+	    pskb_expand_head(skb, HH_DATA_ALIGN(needed - skb_headroom(skb)),
+			     0, GFP_ATOMIC))
+		return -needed;
+
+	ipv6h = skb_push(skb, needed);
 	ip6_flow_hdr(ipv6h, 0, ip6_make_flowlabel(dev_net(dev), skb,
 						  t->fl.u.ip6.flowlabel,
 						  true, &t->fl.u.ip6));
 	ipv6h->hop_limit = t->parms.hop_limit;
 	ipv6h->nexthdr = NEXTHDR_GRE;
 	ipv6h->saddr = t->parms.laddr;
 	ipv6h->daddr = t->parms.raddr;
 
 	p = (__be16 *)(ipv6h + 1);
 	p[0] = ip_tunnel_flags_to_be16(t->parms.o_flags);
 	p[1] = htons(type);
 
 	/*
 	 *	Set the source hardware address.
 	 */
 
 	if (saddr)
 		memcpy(&ipv6h->saddr, saddr, sizeof(struct in6_addr));
 	if (daddr)
 		memcpy(&ipv6h->daddr, daddr, sizeof(struct in6_addr));
 	if (!ipv6_addr_any(&ipv6h->daddr))
 		return t->hlen;
 
 	return -t->hlen;
 }

needed = t->hlen + sizeof(*ipv6h);
if (skb_headroom(skb) < needed &&

<text>
Reason:
The fix calculates the required headroom (needed) and checks if the current headroom is sufficient. If not, it expands the skb headroom via pskb_expand_head() before calling skb_push(). The expansion request is aligned to HH_DATA_ALIGN to meet hardware alignment requirements. If expansion fails, the function returns a negative value indicating the header length needed, allowing callers to handle the error gracefully.
</text>
